headerDisplay: Turns Peloton workouts into HomeKit sensors so automations can run when a workout starts, ends, or reaches a heart-rate zone. Set up in two steps: connect your Peloton account, then add a trigger for what you want to automate. Save, restart Homebridge, and use the sensor in a HomeKit automation. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Peloton Interactive. Uses Peloton's undocumented member API, which can change without notice.
footerDisplay: After saving, restart Homebridge. Your sensors appear in the Home app. Open Automations, choose a sensor as the trigger, and pick what should happen when a workout starts.

name.title: Name
name.description: Shown in Homebridge logs and as the bridge name in the Home app.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Sign in as the membership owner and every household profile appears here. Each member connects their own profile before it is polled.

id.title: Account id
id.description: Generated by the settings page when the account is added and never shown. The stored sign-in is filed under it, so keep it stable.

email.title: Email
email.description: The email address of the Peloton account.

password.title: Password
password.description: Stored in your Homebridge config. The plugin keeps a session token so you rarely need to sign in again. Leave empty for an account connected with Sign in with browser.

userId.title: Peloton user id
userId.description: Filled in by the plugin after the first successful connection.

displayName.title: Display name
displayName.description: Shown in Homebridge logs. Filled in from the Peloton profile when empty.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: Each trigger is a sensor in the Home app. It turns on while its condition is true and off when it stops, so one sensor gives you both a start and an end automation. Each trigger needs a different name.

id.title: Trigger id
id.description: Generated by the settings page when the trigger is added and never shown. The HomeKit accessory is tied to it, so renaming the trigger keeps its automations.

type.title: Trigger type
type.description: Workout is on while a workout is in progress. Heart-rate zone is on while heart rate is at or above a zone.

name.title: Name
name.description: Shown in the Home app. Letters, numbers, spaces and apostrophes. Another trigger may not use the same name.

accessory.title: Show in HomeKit as
accessory.description: Occupancy sensor is on while the condition is true. Switch behaves the same but appears as a toggle.

who.title: Who
who.description: "anyone" for anyone on this membership, or the Peloton user id of one member. A heart-rate zone trigger needs one member; zones come from this member's Peloton profile.

device.title: Device
device.description: Bike is a ride on the Bike or Bike+, Tread is a workout on the Tread or Tread+.

holdAfterEnd.title: Keep on after the workout ends (seconds)
holdAfterEnd.description: Holds the sensor on briefly so stacked classes do not turn your scene off between them.

zone.title: Zone at or above
zone.description: The sensor is on while heart rate is in this zone or a higher one.

holdTime.title: Hold time (seconds)
holdTime.description: The zone must hold this long before the sensor changes, so lights do not flicker on a sprint.

polling.title: Polling
polling.description: How often the plugin asks Peloton what is happening.

fastSwitch.title: Create a Fast polling switch in HomeKit
fastSwitch.description: Turn this switch on from a HomeKit automation right before a workout, for example when the gym light comes on. While it is on, the plugin checks every account quickly, locks onto the first workout it sees, and follows it to the end. Turn it off when the light goes off.

fastSwitchName.title: Name
fastSwitchName.description: Turns itself off automatically after the period set under Advanced.

fastInterval.title: Fast (seconds)
fastInterval.description: While the switch is on or a workout is in progress. Fast polling cannot go below 5 seconds.

standbyInterval.title: Standby (seconds)
standbyInterval.description: When the switch is off. Set to 0 to stop polling entirely until the switch turns on. Use 0 to stop polling, or 30 seconds or more.

calloutDismissed.title: Automation callout dismissed
calloutDismissed.description: Set by the settings page when the Works best with an automation callout is closed.

not.description: With no fast polling switch and standby at 0 the plugin would never poll. Turn one of them back on.

fastSwitchAutoOffMinutes.title: Fast polling switch turns off after (minutes)
fastSwitchAutoOffMinutes.description: Counted from the later of the switch turning on and the last workout ending.

attentionSensor.title: Attention needed sensor
attentionSensor.description: Create an occupancy sensor that turns on when any account needs to be reconnected. Use it in an automation to get a notification.

dailyCheckIn.title: Daily check-in time
dailyCheckIn.description: Once a day the plugin refreshes each account's session and heart-rate zones, even when nobody is working out.

debug.title: Debug logging
debug.description: Log every poll and the workout data it returns. Sign-in details and session tokens are never logged.
